chapter: Looking back and the lean years
title: Playing pretty and playing jazz, and being called a Dixieland player
summary: He always wanted both, recalls practising in the library lecture room, and says Condon-band ballad medleys shocked audiences; he prefers swing.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: No - well, it means you don't have a thought of your own-- and I always had an idea of how I'd like to sound; I can remember once when I was in the library where I was raised, there was a room in the library called a lecture Room - and it had a little podium where the people that write books used to come and lecture to women or men about their new books and I used to go in there and-- with my cornet when I first started playing the coronet - I used to go in there - when there wasn't anybody looking - I'd get up and play my horn and take a little bow and my grandfather used to catch me doing that once in awhile and embarrass the hell out of me, but I think I always had an idea of how I wanted to express myself and I've always been torn between playing pretty and playing jazz and I think I have actually developed both because I find it very gratifying in the middle of a jazzy set of songs, if I play a pretty ballad it always go over with the people because it's--- I suppose some people can't do that - play two different ways--
Is the playing pretty - it just seems to me that you have emphasized that more as you got older---
Well, I love to play melodies--
Yeah, I know that but now, you've got to answer that question now--- (laughter) --
What -- I don't get the question--
In other words, I think that you were in your 40's and 50's before you really began to play a lot of so-called pretty songs - am I wrong about that?
Well, no - we used to do that around Chicago---

Not as much, of course; but we used to do medley-- and the Conden band did the medleys-- starting off - trombone take his favorite song - the clarinet would take his favorite pretty song; I'd take my pretty song and piano had his pretty song and so on -- and it always went over -- it was kind of a little shock treatment to the audience after blasting out some song that was loud and fast.

Yes, it seems as though there were so few people who could do both and sometimes - I used to start to feel bad about being called a Dixieland horn player -- when I knew I could do other things and first of all, my first even though I went through all the Dixieland days and eras and you must remember, I played with big bands and, uh, also, that I like Swing better and, you know, my feeling would be more like the old Benny Goodman band - now, that's the kind of music I like, you see and I always did; I dig every record he ever made and anybody who had a swing band - I got them all -- all those old 78's.
